problem:
What is the minor of ${t}_{33}$ in the matrix
$T=[\begin{aligned}y-x & x & {y}^{2} \\ -x & y+x & 1 \\ {x}^{2} & {y}^{2} & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]?$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Minor in a 3x3 Matrix With Variable Entries
examples.problem:
What is the minor of $c_{22}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & 0 & -3y \\ 1 & x+2y & 4 \\ -y & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & ∗ & -3y \\ ∗ & x+2y & ∗ \\ -y & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =7x\cdot 5-(-3y)\cdot (-y) \\  & =35x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
For the matrix
$Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$
find the minor ${M}_{32}$ of the entry ${y}_{32}.$

${M}_{32}=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The minor of ${y}_{32}=-1$ (third row, second column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-1$ are removed: 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ & 5 \\ 3 & ∗ & 0 \\ ∗ & -1 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${y}_{32}=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{32} & =\text{det}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1)\cdot 0-3\cdot 5 \\  & =0-15 \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$
